maya (PM): Quick thread: sketching a compact "week0 rapid-groom" playbook. Goal: make day-0 decisions consistent — who gets immediate fixes, what eats the risk budget, and how support tags escalate. Posting concise rules + ask for objections.

liam (ENG): +1. Can we define "risk budget" in practical terms? how many hotfix deploys allowed before we pause new feature releases?

ben (Data): suggest tangible metric: max 3 emergency deploys (hotfixes or rollbacks) per major feature in week0, or error-spike events totalling >30min during business hours -> risk budget exhausted. We can track via incident windows.

otto (SRE): severity mapping quick proposal:
- Sev0: data loss/corruption or total outage -> page, immediate hotpatch
- Sev1: critical feature broken for >1% active users or paying customers -> 48h hotfix target, canary if possible
- Sev2: degraded UX or partial failures with workaround -> schedule in weekly fix batch
- Sev3: polish/enhancement -> backlog
Add: if risk budget exhausted, default to conservative posture: freeze non-essential deploys.

yara (Support): tagging template for support to use (short):
"""
Subject: brief error title
Steps to reproduce:
Number of customers affected (estimate):
Client/app version/region:
Attach screenshot/console logs:
"""
If support uses this exact block, triage is much faster.

rachel (Design): note on UX: call out "core-flow" tags (signup, billing, API auth). Any core-flow regression should be auto-promoted to Sev1. For UI bugs, require screenshot + minimal repro. Quick CSS fixes ok for Sev1 if they restore flow.

claire (ProdOps): labels and boards: propose lanes: week0:hotfix, week0:deferred, week0:enhancement. Use labels: week0:sev0|sev1|sev2|sev3 + customer:ID. We'll automate creation from support-bot when two similar tickets hit in 6h.

liam (ENG): fastlane process: for Sev0/1 -> tag fastlane-review, 2 reviewers + oncall approval in 6h. Merge + canary deploy 5% traffic for 15m. Rollback threshold: error rate >50% or latency 95p > SLA by 2x -> immediate rollback.

ben (Data): automation alert thresholds we can wire into triage board: new error signature >0.5% requests; crash cluster >3 customers in 1h; feature usage drop >25% for 30m. Any trigger auto-creates a draft with suggested severity.

otto (SRE): canary rule clarified: 5% for 20m with health checks (error-rate, p95 latency, basic synthetic checks). If infra can't do canary, require blue-green with 15m observation window.

maya (PM): proposal for conversion rule bug -> enhancement: only allowed if all are true: non-ambiguous workaround exists, affects <0.5% DAU, no data risk, and no contractual SLA impact. Otherwise keep as bug.

liam (ENG): small ask: add a short fast-review checklist in PR template: link to issue, repro steps, smoke test steps, rollback plan. I'll draft.

claire (ProdOps): I'll set up the lanes and label automation today. Also will pin a tiny checklist in the board: reproduce, attach logs, assign owner, ETA, notify customers if Sev0/1.

yara (Support): will start using template now and will add customer:ID when available.

triage-bot: Rule created: W0-01-auto-create when support-template matched twice in 6h. Linked to oncall rotation.

maya (PM): action items (compact):
- liam: PR fastlane template + reviewer checklist (tomorrow AM)
- ben: dashboard card with risk-budget counters and alert feeds (EOD)
- claire: create week0 lanes + automation (today)
- rachel: mini UI patch guidance for Sev1 (EOD)
- otto: add canary/rollback rules to runbook (today)
- yara: enforce support template (immediate)

liam (ENG): tiny automation snippet for labeling (pseudo):
```
# pseudo
support-bot create-issue --body @support-template && support-bot tag --add week0:sev1
```

maya (PM): if no objections I'll pin this thread and run a 10-min sync tomorrow 09:30 to walk through playbook. We want consistent triage and minimal churn for eng. :calendar: :white_check_mark:
